reviewText: This was a gift for my other husband.  He's making us things from it all the time and we love the food.  Directions are simple, easy to read and interpret, and fun to make.  We all love different kinds of cuisine and Raichlen provides recipes from everywhere along the barbecue trail as he calls it. Get it and just open a page.  Have at it.  You'll love the food and it has provided us with an insight into the culture that produced it. It's all about broadening horizons.  Yum!!

This is a very nice spreader.  It feels very solid and the pneumatic tires give it great maneuverability and handling over bumps.  The control arm is solid metal, not a cable, which gives you precise control and will last a long time.  The settings take some experimentation with your various products to get it right, but that is true of any spreader.  It has good distribution... probably flings material a little farther on the right side than the left, but it is far more even than my crappy Edgeguard ever was.

The metal base with the hose attachments is very poorly designed and made. As the previous reviewer pointed out, it leaks badly and just pops off. There is no way to fix or tighten this junction and when the plastic wears a bit the hose just falls off and sprinkler is useless.AVOID ANY GILMOUR Sprinklers with this spike base. The sprinkler heads themselves work fairly well.

For the most part this works pretty good. I bought the John Deere and this one, they both work the same. This is the first time I am waterin my lawn, so to me it seems like they use a lot of water, especially in narrow areas. They are better made for large areas, for narrow corridors, use some other system.

This hose is supposed to be flexible.  Its hard, heavy and unwieldy.  I don't know if it kinks or not, because I could tell, as soon as I removed it from the box, that I would have to return it.  If you want a lightweight, soft hose (and I know they exist because I have one), do not buy this thing.

This tool works very well for cutting brush and woody stemmed weeds up to about 2". It will work for larger brush and small trees with multiple swings but I find it easier to use a bow saw for the occasional larger plants I encounter. Note that if you need to cut a lot of larger brush a brush hook would be better than this ditch bank blade as the brush hook blade is thicker and heavier.The tool needs to be sharpened right out of the package to perform best. This removes the paint and any nicks and burrs from the factory grinding as well shipping and handling nicks. I resharpen the blades and spray them with WD-40 after each use so it remains rust free and is ready to go for the next session of cutting brush. Also, I suggest installing either lock washers or nyloc nuts on the bolts to keep them tight in use. Even with that, check them after each use to make sure they are tight--it seems that initially the ash handle compresses a bit and the metal side plates need time to seat fully into the ash.This tool has been a huge improvement over my large lopping shears and machette for clearing brush on a new rail trail.Great tool if used appropriately. Per the package it can also be used to ward off zombies and the undead but I've not had that need to date.

This product is a typical, yet usable, B&D design. The handle-mounted power cord lock is somewhat difficult to use, but works fairly well after the cord is "locked" into a type of holder that could be improved. The product does what it is intended to do, no more, no less.  It is a powerful vacuum and works very well with high amounts of dry leaf material.  The attached bagger is somewhat cumbersome to use and empty, produces copious amounts of leaf-dust, but overall, this product works quite well in vacuuming lots of leaf and yard material.

I was excited to ditch my $1.99, two-prong corn holders for this corkscrew design but regret it. The corkscrew design twists into the end of the corn. I thought this was a genius idea but the problem is that the prong continues to twist when in the corn. Since it doesn't have a second prong to prevent the pivoting, the corn will flip and slip all around the prong, which is super annoying when trying to butter and eat. The storage case and grips are nice but I think the design itself is problematic. I'll be ditching these and going back to a two-prong approach.
summary: Seems Like Good Idea But Problematic

reviewText: I purchased the Leaf Hog last year and was very impressed with it.  It helped reduce the time to take care of leaves from about 80 hours of work to about 35 hours and my back didn't hurt nearly as much last year.  This year I tried out the Leaf Collection system as much of the time I spent last year was dumping out the leaf collection bag to mulch more until the garbage can was full.  On this go around I had 4 - 55 gallon garbage cans and started mulching the big piles I had.  I would just mulch until a can was full, move the fabric over to the next can and continue.  This sped up my time to finishing in under 20 hours this year.I would highly recommend it if you need to mulch more than a single bag full.  It saved a ton of time for me and I have no doubt it can do the same for you.

Never used a manual lawnmower. Need to adjust heigth of back roller. If you have a small area then its fine. You will need a trimmer though for edges and difficult areas. May have to go over the area twice to make the cut even

Good price. Good product. I had read some poor reviews of competitive products before purchasing this one, so I was a little concerned. But the Flowtron turned out to be exactly what I was looking for.

I have owned the Flowtron BK-15D for about nine months now. I have it hanging at the corner ceiling of my room. The power plug of the bug lamp is connected to a 24 hour digital programmable timer (Intermatic DT121) set to automatically turn on the bug lamp at night, then turn off in the morning. Underneath the bug lamp is a litter tray with a mixture of baking soda and beach sand. I have had no problems with the bug lamp. There are times when I am woken up from sleep because of bugs being zapped, but after a while, you can get used to that zapping sound. Last year, prior to owning the bug lamp, I have had spider bites, gnat infestations, wandering moths, and mosquitoes in my room. With the Flowtron BK-15D, my room and bed is now bug-free. No more expenses toward bug sprays and rash ointments. As far as cleaning and maintaining the bug lamp, I have had no need to do this as I have set up a litter tray lined with a mixture of fine sand and baking soda, which I periodically empty and refill. In the future, I would probably spray the interior of the lamp housing with compressed air and brush off dead bugs stuck on the metal casing, but other than that, the lamp is extremely low maintenance. I would recommend this product to people who are in my situation: cost effective mosquito control for a private space or room.

I had "won" a similar product at a family reunion and used it for many things. Most recently, I used it to tie my grape vines to supporting stakes. When I ran out, I couldn't find them locally and was so happy to find them available through Amazon.The wire tie makes these strong and the plastic coating makes them good for indoor or outdoor use. So much better than reusing the paper covered ties that come on grocery store products. Highly recommended.
The birds ate all of our blueberries last year, so this year we decided to invest in some netting as a repellent. It is working like a charm. I'm going out to pick the ripe berries tonight.

Bought last summer.  Researching reel mowers, this is the only one I could find that would adjust the cut height.  (Most reel mowers do not adjust AND cut the grass very short, which is bad for each the lawn and the environment-excessive watering required)  I have a small lawn, in town.  50'x60'.  This mower is easy to use/operate (little effort).  Never worry about engine maintenance or having gas or using gas (environment).  Also, of course, it is incredibly quiet.  These mowers do struggle with tall grass or weeds.  If you let the lawn go, it will not cut tall grass.  I enjoy my mower a great deal.  I let the grass get too long on vacation last year and borrowed a gas mower when I returned.  I feel great about the environment and myself every time I use it.

I knew I had a mouse in the basement and wanted to use a humane way to catch it.  I used the trap with just a little peanut butter as some reviewers have advised, and for a couple of weeks absolutely nothing happened (even as the fresh evidence of the mouse continued to mount all around it) to the point that I was ready to dismiss it as ineffective;  then one day I happened to glance at the trap and saw it had "sprung".  No movement from inside, but it felt a bit heavier than it should have if empty, so I steeled myself for the possibility of finding a starved-to-death mouse carcass inside...or having a live mouse jump out at me...okay, actually I had my son open the trap, well away from the house...apparently the mouse was alive and well, and is now living somewhere else.  Happy ending.One minor criticism--it would have been helpful if there had been a way to see inside the trap and know for sure if it contained a mouse, and what the mouse's condition might be.  I don't think I'd have been nervous about opening the trap if I'd had some way of knowing what to expect, and it doesn't seem as though it would be difficult to make a transparent window in the side of the trap for that purpose.
I was a little worried after reading about so many different chain sizes for my Homelite saw. This one fits well and seems to be at least as good as the original.
I have used this brand for a long time now and the Hummingbirds will drain a 2 cup feeder in less than 2 weeks.  They love it!

I actually do not own the current model of the Weber Genesis grill--mine is ten years old and still going strong.  I live in the Pacific Northwest and I use my grill all year around--rain, snow or shine.  I only found out recently that my oven broiler (which was new three years ago) did not work, because I use my grill instead of the oven.  These grills are made to last.  I have never grilled anything that was not done perfectly.  Even  though it is nice to have something new and shiny, I cannot justify replacing my Genesis 4000 as long as it is working.  I started my grilling experience with the Weber kettle grill and would still be using that if I had not received my gas grill for my birthday 10 years ago.  I passed the kettle down to my nephew and he is still using it.  You cannot go wrong with this product. Is is one of the few things manufactured today that is truly of high quality--made to last.
Just what I  expected, it works great and is the perfect size for my husband and myself to use. Thank you
I have always loved Weber and this is no different.Best material for grilling. easy setup,easy cleanup. Cant say enough about this! LOVE it!

I purchased this trap when I was battling groundhogs who saw my garden as a buffet.  I had originally purchased 2 traps from Tractor Supply, but they weren't living up.  The traps were made poorly and the groundhogs were able to pound the cage until the wire came loose and they were able to escape.I did some research and Havahart was getting a high rating.  I purchased this trap and I didn't go wrong.  Nothing is escaping this baby.  It's strong enough to hold the groundhogs and the door is easy to open when you release them.  I will be replacing another Tractor Supply cage this summer with this Havahart.  I highly recommend it.

On the plus side, was fairly easy to put together and doesn't take up too much storage space if you remove the bag/hang it on a wall.  But as other reviewers have said, you have to adjust the height and hold/push the sweeper at just the right angle to get it to pick up.  Once you get the hang of it, though, you're only going to get a small area done at a time before the bag fills up.  In the end, it took just as long to clear an area as it does to use a rake because of all the stopping to empty the bag. I didn't have much luck removing the bag and emptying that way (into a paper lawn bag...), so basically you have to take all the leaves out by hand. Would only recommend if you really can't handle the twisting and turning involved in raking...and have no problem bending and picking up piles of leaves.
They don't work as good as it says...I would not buy this product again...It does not control fleas or other bugs like it says...It is a waste of money...Don't buy this!

I am very happy with this scythe. It cuts easily through most weeds, which is great because that's what I bought it for. It doesn't cut through grass as easily, but that's OK with me, because most of the areas that I need to trim are overgrown weeds. You just have to work a bit harder to cut through tall grasses - in case that's what you are looking to use it for. Using the scythe is good exercise, too - but it's not enough to get you really winded (unless you're kind of out of shape). I actually bought two of these scythes - one to keep in the front yard, and one to keep in the back yard. Turns out that was a good thing, because my (14 year old) son and my (12 year old) nephew (who is visiting us for the summer) had a great time using them to cut back some of the weeds in my back yard. I just made sure they understood that they could NOT work ANYWHERE NEAR EACH OTHER, for safety's sake. It's the first time my son has actually volunteered to help with the yard work. I guess using a garden tool (e.g. a scythe) which also doubles as a weapon on some of his video games was the secret to his interest. Or, to steal a concept from Rita Rudner - "teenage boys will do yardwork, when there's danger involved". Oh, well - whatever their reason, the boys really like using these scythes; and so do I. I highly recommend them for a healthy way to trim your weeds without having to struggle with the nylon fishing line (which always tangles up on me and/or breaks) or electrical cords (that never seem to reach far enough) on one of those electric weed-wackers!
Programmed right out of the box without reading the instructions. Great features and room to expand. Especially like the individual zone watering option.
Arrived in a timely manner.  Quality tool. As advertised.
It's very handy, has a great size when cultivating herbs. So far I have no cons, and the price was good.
Amazing. I am 69, 5'6",  and the 36" version works very well for me, far better than the old splitting maul it replaced. I have been splitting ash with it for a month now, and am very pleased
It's all the good things people say! I could even cut through some gnarly twisted wood that I thought would be impossible!

I've had a number of pulsating sprinklers over the years, and they have always had some plastic parts that just don't hold up.  This one is VERY WELL made and has been used several seasons.  It's just as good as new.  Covers a lot of territory and is easy to adjust.  Recommend it.

Terrible pun I know but this thing is awesome! First test was with steak, sausage and bacon and it was absolutely amazing! I really wasn't expecting the intense smokey flavors that came out of this. It began leaking smoke a bit about half way through the process but a slight tweaking of the lid cut it down to almost nothing. Can't wait to find more things to smoke!!

I've owned the same Patio Caddie for over 10 years now!  It grills beautifully over clay briquettes, giving that great smoke flavor and does it all on a fraction of the propane.  The key to getting lots of heat from a tiny burner is cooking COVERED.  I even bought a kit to retrofit the burner plate and made the old grill like new again for $20!It's a small grill, but will cook six large steaks all at once.
Have used this brand/type before with great success but for some reason the ones I've ordered recently don't attract the flys.

reviewText: If you are in the market for this type of smoker, do your self a favor and get this one. I owned two different bullet-style water smokers before this one, and neither of them compared. This one keeps the heat in much better, and isn't built as crappy as just about all the other ones. The reason is, this one is one solid cylinder, and all the parts fit nicely together. All the other ones are assembled from one piece of sheet metal, which never fits the top or bottom pieces. Go with the Weber Smokey Mountain.

Bought them with idea for some slip on shoes for garden and saturday generally. they are made of a tough and not very flexible plastic. there is no cushion to them at all. good treads and look ok but very uncomfortable so far. Ive had them 3 days. Ive never had plastic shoes/clogs so i dont know if they break in or what. But if they dont get more comfortable, theyre going in the garbage or to resale. In fact two of my neighbors came over to see my new toy and they took it home and did their roofs in minutes. I like the fact that the handles can be taken apart for easy storage or I can take it to my cabin.I recommend it to anyone. I'm 68 and it is so easy to use.Great Product!

This shovel is quite heavy, but it deserves 5 stars as even so, its still of such good quality, that it doesn't matter.  Used it several times this year. This feeder has allowed me to finally attract hummingbirds to my office window! (I'd tried numerous other models.) I have started a small garden in the hydrofarm.  It was easy to set up.  The pump is a little noisy so you don't want it in a bedroom.  I so far have harvested salad greens.  Now I'm working on trying to grow swiss chard, tomatoes, and green beans.  It is a fun hobby.  I am doing better with this then when I grow plants from seeds in dirt.

I bought this using a gift certificate from work. I  had been looking at metal detectors for a few months and this one quickly rises to the top of the list for entry level and low cost. It's very light weight but reasonably well constructed. There are just enough settings to make it very effective and it's still easy to setup and use. It works very well for shallow to moderately deep targets (1-4 inches) and finds targets well below that when they are larger. The tone setting with disc. set at about 2 o'clock position is very effective for coin shooting. The unit is very sensitive to small targets as deep as 6 inches in the all metal mode. overall I've been very satisfied with this machine and I feel it's the best value for a metal detector in this price range. this one gets my "best bang for the Buck" award.

(See the photo of my usual grumpy husband Jeff, who hates mowing the lawn, hogging it all for himself with glee.) This little Black & Decker is light and nimble and just about the best darn lawn mower we ever owned. So there.And what's best, each time you pause, you can just let go of the handle and the mower shuts off. No energy waster, this one, so you'll save on your electric bill big time. Pull on the handle and you're back in business. No tugging on any backbreaking cords till sweat beads on your brow. Or a cold beer.Okay, maybe not a cold beer. But still.

reviewText: Plastair SpringJet 50-Foot Coiled Water Hose and Wand Set, Ocean Blue #PUJ250B93OTThe picture clearly shows brass or metal faucet connectors on the product, but what I received has not just plastic, but cheap plastic connectors. The plastic connector flexes when tighened on the faucet and leaks immensely. When tighened more, it leaks more because it flexes and separates from the internal hose component.  Even if you can tolerate the leaking, if you tug any at all on the hose it will pull through the cheap plastic connector on the faucet separating it from the connector and the faucet.  Unless one is interested in wasting huge amounts of water, I cannot recommend this product to anyone as it is totally unusable.

The motion activated sprinkler sounded like a good idea for keeping the deer out of our flower gardens. We installed two and set our game camera to record the fun. Three days later we checked the camera and found the sprinklers activating time after time with no animal or other triggering event present. Then the major disappointment. We watched a full grown deer walk right past the front of the sprinkler and start grazing on our flowers, again. The scarecrow did nothing. Boxed them back up and returned for a refund.
summary: Ran constantly except when a deer was present

Update: 2 years ago I found the splitter had lost 2 quarts of oil. I looked for a leak, and rationed that I probably lost the oil because the ground is uneven and the rudimentary air hole in the oil plug lets oil out if it is pointed down hill.I added oil and worked the summer. At the end of the summer, same story, several quarts low. I added more oil and did not observe any leak while it was running, but did observe oil under the oil tank.This year I let it to my nephew who brought it back to my house and I put it in my garage. Voila, I saw an oil leak. Using a light I found the leak was a 1.5" crack in the tank under the engine. I contacted Troy Bilt and told them what I told you. They will not warranty this work and told me to take it to a certified Troy Bilt repair center who quoted me nearly $800 to repair it.It is unfortunate this company does not support customers any better than this. Had I put this splitter on concrete two years ago, I would have found the leak while still under warranty. Even though I reported the leaking oil occurred during the warranty period, and only found the leak last week, they still won't warranty it. This is sad because Troy Bilt used to be something you could buy with confidence, but apparently not anymore. There are too many reports of inadequate welds and cracking tanks to recommend this splitter to anyone. Certainly the hydraulics still work good, but a leaking tank is just plain a bad idea.PaulWhen I researched log splitters, I settled on Troy-Bilt. I examined three models and chose the 33 ton splitter for its power, design and of course the reputation Troy-Bilt has. It comes with a Honda 8 HP engine, which on other slitters is an expensive upgrade.I read the review about it being shipped in parts. I ordered it and found the instructions to actually being helpful. Very well thought out and engineered, I put it together in about 4.5 hours, from the time I opened the crate to when I split the first log. I recommend this to anyone who is interested in a splitter and Amazon's price is the best on the market. I do recommend you have an assistant in putting it together, although one person can assemble it. Please note you also need 8 gallons of hydraulic fluid, not seven. You have to allow for the hoses, cylinder, and filter.I finally got a chance to use it on some 24-30 inch dried cottonwood logs. Impressive is all I have to say. Cottonwood tears, not splits and the family splitter couldn't touch this stuff. This splitter tore right threw it. When it hit nasty narly wood, the ram slowed down and continued on. The auto return feature also is a nice touch, it retracts while you get another piece. I have no regrets and look forward to taking it out in the spring to split the other 10 - 12 cords of hardwood. Right now there is 3 feet of snow on the ground so this will unfortunately have to wait until spring.
I am pleased with my purchase and recommend it to someone looking to do light garden work or replanting a lawn

Brussel's DT0117ALW Hawaiian Umbrella Tree in Water Pot Bonsai:  I received it as a gift from my daughter.  It was easy to set up.  The only problem was when I first placed the white stones, I put them in the water area instead of in the drain tray.  The drain tray with the white stones in it allows the water to be slowly absorbed thus protecting and prolonging the life of the tree.  I have had it for a month and it didn't loose any leaves as reported that it might.  I bought a little misting bottle for daily soft mists and monitor the tray's white stones.  If I can't see water in the stones I add a little water.  Love the plant!

The instructions were clear as how to hang this properly, and installation time took less than two minutes.It is holding a 10 inch pot of geraniums and it was easy to attach to the fence post. reviewText: After my long lasting Troy-Built push lawn mower died, I decided to buy a new one instead of getting it fixed.  After reading and researching on-line reviews for self-propelled lawn mowers it seemed they started in the price range around $300.  I had never had a self-propelled mower before.  But, the thought that if the wife or kids wanted to volunteer mowing our small yard a self-propelled mower would make it a more enjoyable experience.Several features I was looking for were: (1) Larger rear wheels, (2) Dependable engine, (3) Decent warranty, (4) Variable speed drive.  This mower has all these except the variable speed, which was not a problem for me since a little downward pressure on the handle will make the front wheels lift off and slow it down if needed.  With the larger rear wheels it seems to accomplish this and turning fairly well.  Also, this is the << ONLY >> mower in this price range that has a dependable HONDA engine.  Looking at the reviews of more expensive mowers, the HONDA engines were a major selling point considering their ease of starting and dependability.  Some of the reviewers here at Amazon had indicated they had problems with that engine.  For the price to value features of this mower, I was willing to take a gamble.This last weekend it was delivered to our doorstep. The time it had taken since my old mower had died and it arrived had been a little over two weeks.  The lawn looked like a jungle and I was in a hurry to get it mowed before the neighbors started to complain.  Probably should have taken the time to read the instructions first before I assembled and started it though.To start off, there were only 4 bolt/wing nuts to make up as a previous reviewer had indicated. A mistake I made was not putting them in the correct direction since the grass collection bag interfered with the lower ones until I turned them 180 degrees about.  The instructions probably would have told me this if I had read them.  Also, the oil that came in the bottle was just a tad more than the capacity of the oil reservoir.  DON'T OVERFILL a gas engine.  Luckily, I checked the dip stick and saw that it was a little overfull after dumping the WHOLE bottle in.  I emptied a little oil out until the dipstick showed the correct level and continued the startup process by filling the gas tank.At that point I had to get the manual out to see a picture of which way the gas shut-off valve should be pointed.  Also, the spark plug wire had to be attached to the spark plug.  OK... ready to fire her up.  I turned the throttle to choke and gave a couple of tugs.  Nothing.  Huh, maybe I got a dud like the previous reviewer on Amazon.  A couple of more uneventful tugs and I realize the carburetor was flooded with gas.  So, I took the air filter off to let the carburetor air out.A few minutes passed and I replaced the air filter.  A couple of more tugs proved uneventful.  Wow, I stood back in thought looking at the new lifeless piece of equipment I had put so much hope and anticipation in.  Then it dawned on me, I may have to hold the top lever on the handle back when I was pulling the starting cord.  I turned the throttle to medium, held one hand on the "kill switch" lever on the handle and pulled the cord.  The engine burst to life!  If only I had taken the time to read all the instructions, I probably would have had a more successful startup.Nah, I knew what I was doing?  Besides I had a jungle to mow.  The jungle is gone now and I am very confident in this machine to perform well for me in the future.  I even went out a couple of days later while writing this review to test it to see if it started again.  I turned the throttle to "choke" and with one tug it started again.  Also, I noticed the throttle move on it's own down to a run position instead of the "choke" position after it started.  Very cool.Who knows maybe the wife and kids will use this thing?  If nothing else, they can start it for me.

It has a nice water, dirt and and clumsy/rough behavior resistant fabric and construction, enough cushion, ergonomic rump molding and tilts plenty far forward, sideways and back (while feeling perfectly safe and stable) to get my garden work done.I did not once feel like I was going to tip or that it was going to fly out from under me.It is incredibly durable and very convenient.  It slid and ground into gravel all spring and summer at least 4 days per week for at least a half day at a session without showing any real wear (even on the bottom plastic).  I shoved weeders,scissors, clippers, hand trowels etc. into the pockets and they are in good condition.  No holes, frays... nothing. I would have been sinking in the dirt and grass, it would not have survived the gravel and this thing (although I am sure they do not recommend it) can scoot easily while still under you. Ok, these traps are fantastic but I have watched certain little baby mice (who are not heavy enough to trigger the trap) eat all of the peanut butter and walk away and then come back for seconds like our porch was Hometown Buffet or something.  Well, years ago I came up with the perfect plan to solve that problem.  I purchased some Contrac rodenticide poison pellet bags and a six pack of these Snap-E traps for a decent price on Ebay (I couldn't find the six pack here) and I caught 9 mice in three days.  I opened the pellet bags and mixed a few of them in with the peanut butter and baited the traps with the mixture. So, even when the baby mice fill up on second and third helpings and then walk away happy.....they won't be walking for long.  For people who don't want to get too close when disposing of the remains, just open a wire hanger to the desired length, hook the trap and hold over the trash can/bag and with the free hand squeeze the silver bar and release the mouse.  It is so easy!!  The traps did catch one little guy but only caught its leg and didn't kill him so after much debate on what to do we decided to take him for a ride out to a field and set him free.  Look, I know he probably doesn't "stand" a chance out there and if they would all jump in my car I would gladly give them a ride to any other place but mine but that's not how life works and they need to go.  So, again, these traps work...PERIOD!!  It's not the trap's fault that some mice are light on their feet.
summary: HERE'S A TIP TO GET THEM ALL!!!!

They only seemed to give me about half the charge I was getting from the plug in chargers, and really choked the power available while riding.  Tried to contact the manufacturer, who basically said they were not intended for the use I have put them to.  Oh well.  Have wired in one of the mppt units at 24 volts, with 4 remaining Sunforce units, and already seeing 4 more volts available under load than with the 6 Sunforce units, and only spending about eight bucks more over all.
summary: over-protective, at a significant expense of available solar power being WASTED.

My boyfriend and I live in a small apartment with no outdoor space and we really missed being able to grill. We purchased the Meco 9309W deluxe grill and could not be happier. In a nutshell, it is one of the best purchases I have ever made. The grill is small enough that we can store it in our apartment. It is unobtrusive and fits so easily in a spare corner that you wouldn't even know it was there. When we want to use it we simply put it out on our (very) small porch and can actually grill from inside. (Note: this is not an indoor grill.)Though the grill is electric, it cooks very much like a gas grill. Depending on what you are cooking, flareups and smoke can occur, but they make the food taste even better. Grease drips into the bottom of the grill, where there is a small hole for drainage. However, you need to put something beneath to catch the excess. I wish that the sellers would supply a small cup to catch the drippings, as there is a space for one, but a cup made of aluminum foil works just as well and is easy to clean up.The Meco grill is well made and cooks wonderfully. I use it several times a week (sometimes twice a day on weekends). It has plenty of space, so I can cook enough meat and vegetables for four or more people simultaneously. I have not yet used the rotisserie feature, but based on my experiences thus far I am sure it would produce great tasting food.For such a wonderful grill, the price was very reasonable; also, grilling has not increased our electric bill, so it seems comparable to using the oven/stove. I love the Meco grill and look forward to many more years with it. I would recommend it to anyone who doesn't have much space or who doesn't want to spend a lot of money on a large grill.
summary: Great Grill at a Great Price

Only now do I realize that Amazon provided virtually no information on the product- so its anybody's guess as to what you are actually ordering.  Given the importance of this feature to proper use of this product, it was absolutely incumbent on Amazon to inform the customer that this critical part would not be included in their order, and they would either have to use the product without this critical part, which would seriously cripple the usefulness of the product- or spend time and money finding the part on their own. This product worked from day one even though I had a small problem trying to figure how to bait the trap. It would be helpful if they gave a little more instruction on the best way to make sure the bait is properly placed. Initially, I was just placing sunflower seeds on the ground and placing the trap over the seeds. That worked fine until one little guy decided it wasn't a good idea to step on the trigger even though there were plenty of seeds beyond it. He/she actually ate all of the seed I put down four times before I finally got smart enough to attach some seeds with peanut butter to the trigger itself. He wasn't smart enough to figure that out. It also might be helpful if there were more holes on the top of the trap in order to bait it without moving it.Other than that, it works wonderfully. I have gotten rid of fourteen, have not seen any more, and my wife is happy that they are still alive and living in a new community 2 miles away.
Be sure you measure the length and with of what you are replacing. Also, this isn't very thick so it might be uncomfortable.

I have had this for about a week and have been using it everyday. So far, it's doing fine, however by examining the product I get a scary feeling that it won't last very long  due to the reviews and examining the material of this product. Yes, it is hard plastic but hard plastic like this product can be easily crack on the cement by accidentally dropping it.  The design of this product I would give it a 3-star. Nothing to brag about it except for the slick and monstrous design it shows. I'm afraid to use this nozzle as a normal everyday-used nozzle because of the material it uses. I have to be very careful of not  dropping this nozzle, however my first modification, I've modify it by placing a weather-proof strip molding inside both of the dipping (where the Made in Italy) hole were, to raise it up so that when I do drop it- it will protect the upper part of the nozzle by those strips. My second modification is that I've installed a plastic ring just around the quick-connect ( the orange part) so it will protect the lower part of this nozzle when drop, because it's raise.(hopefully) Both upper and lower part of this nozzle is protected by my modification when is drop. I'm hoping that it will help last the life of this nozzle. Good luck!!!

The filter works well and is easy to install. My only problem was a cracked pedestal base. And I can see why it happened. The packaging is very poor and the main tank beats the base during shipping. However, Amazon paid me for a replacement ($50) so it worked out fine. Shipping was reasonably fast. It only took about one week even though I opted for the "free" shipping.The multi-port valve plumbing was completely different from my old filter (StaRite) and I had to re-plumb the pump inlet, outlet and waste ports. I used 150 lbs of Zeobrite instead of 300 lbs of sand because the Zeo has finer filtering characteristics. The filter comes with a new pressure gauge which seems to be a cut above in quality. The site glass in the multi-port head is nice for viewing the dirty water when backwashing. I had to use a lot of teflon tape on the 1 1/2" port threads or they would leak. Seems like the threads may be straight and the PVC parts at the hardware stores are slightly tapered. The filter has been in use for one month and so far, no problems.  With the exception of the base, everything appears to be of high quality construction.

And six months after purchase the o-rings that are in the joint have disintegrated and broken. I will try to permanently seal the joint with some silicone sealant.  I don't care if it's locked in one position.  The "Pour & Store" is a gimmick anyway.I hope others had a better experience.

This saw cuts through tree limbs so incredibly fast - it is unreal.  I have a ~35 fully size pine trees on my property, and I always reach for this saw when I need it.  I have small electric powered chainsaw too, but honestly this Corona hand-saw cuts through 3, 4, 5 and 6-inch diameter limbs so quickly with such a small amount of effort that I hardly ever reach for the chainsaw.  It cuts on both the push and pull strokes to double the cutting speed, and the curved action really helps the forward and back strokes "catch" even better.  On the forward stroke, the back part of the blade closest to the handle really digs in, and then on the backward stroke, the curve makes the front teeth on the blade really dig in.  I have had mine for about 4 years, and can't tell you how much use it has gotten all-the-while the blade seems as sharp as the day I got it, and I have done no maintenance to it whatsoever.  I've never sharpened the teeth, and I have given this thing a beating and it hasn't declined in performance at all!  Even with pine sap along the side of the blade, this thing hasn't had the slightest amount of rust anywhere on it.  It looks like I will probably get another 20 years out of this incredible saw, as it's holding up better than I could have ever imagined.Seriously, it's 20-seconds and probably 20 full strokes to rip through a 4-inch diameter limb.It travels so well too.  It is as light as just 1 pound probably.  I kept the cardboard blade cover.  You can grab this saw and walk around the yard with hardly even noticing that you're carrying it.  The shape makes it well balanced, and it isn't awkward at all while climbing ladders.I have used it cutting for hours straight, regularly just throwing it to the ground after a cut, and the red handle makes it so easy to find among the cut brush.
summary: This Corona Clipper Saw Rips Through Limbs

reviewText: We seem to get mosquito's year round (No Cal. Bay Area with many vineyards nearby) and purchased this product last fall. reviewText: I had been looking for a cart bigger than the standard small model but smaller than the standard big model. This was it. But it is not quite as large as the listing says, those dimensions are the size of the shipping box! Take off about an inch for length and width. We are using the cart to move railroad tie landscaping barriers (170 lbs each) around the back yard. It does that with ease. I wouldn't call anything on this cart is flimsy. It is sturdy, maneuverable and versatile. All four of the tires required additional air pressure which can only be done with a manual pump per the users manual. But I used my electric emergency tire pump from the trunk of my car. Just keep in mind that due to the low volume of air in the tires they fill up fast - don't go to the gas station! There is a little confusion about the correct psi for the tires (manual says one thing and tires sidewall says another). Use the lower. Shipping box arrived in OK condition, not perfect. But there were no parts missing. Assembly takes awhile (and more tools than the manual states - screw driver and plyers aren't going to get the job done). Ratchet set needed if you don't want a "repetitive motion injury"! But beyond all of that, its a good cart.Recommended by us!Enjoy

I am very happy with it so far - it is so sturdy that I can't ever imagine it breaking.  I love that it comes with both the solid and liquid injectors. It's easy to switch between the two, and it's very simple to take apart for cleaning.  The extra cost is worth it- don't waste your money on plastic injectors!  Highly recommended.As far as the usefulness of the product itself- these flavor injectors make a huge difference in the quality of the food.  I've used them for turkeys, picnic ham/pulled pork, and whole chickens, and every time I use it the meat turns out very flavorful and perfectly cooked.  It helps prevent the meat from drying out while cooking.  I will use it for every dish if I can.Just a note about the seller, Grady's Online- they are a bit slow. It took them four business days to ship my package, and it was first class so it took another week to arrive.  A positive experience otherwise, but if you think you're going to need this item you should buy it now rather than wait until the last minute.

reviewText: We recently purchased the Outdoor Residential Controller with Cloud Technology and have been very impressed thus far with its capabilities.  Our reasoning for purchasing this controller is we have two homes.  Our primary home is on the east coast and the home we wanted to use the new controller on is in our residence in Arizona.  Our main purpose for such a controller was to have the ability for our landscaper to adjust our watering schedule on the fly and for us to monitor those changes remotely.  We also wanted the ability to know the amount of water our landscape uses.When we purchased the controller, we had only a week to install and test the unit before we needed to return to the east coast. We initially  tested the unit with the gateway indoors and it communicated perfectly.  However, once we placed the unit outside, made the connections and turned it on, the display failed.  We contacted Cyber-Rain and explained what happened and also told them that we were under a time crunch to  get the unit install along with a  flow sensor and test it before we left.  Due to the time crunch, they overnighted a new controller.  Their sales and support staff answered all questions on the flow sensor and the installation of the controller.The controller and flow sensor work just as we had hoped.  Our landscaper can program the watering needs of our shrubs and trees.  We can remotely check the water flow and usage, as well as how often our plants are being watered.  We are very pleased with our purchase and would highly recommend this controller.
summary: Cyber-Rain Outdoor Residential Controller w/Cloud Technology

I bought a DuroMax 10,000 Watt Generator from [...]  Model #XP10000e a while ago and have never had to use it up until now. It is capable of 120 volt operation and or 220 volt operation.Many people have told me that it's not possible to get simultaneous 240 & 120 from the generator but I'm here to tell you that it is possible and works extremely well.After some trial and error I figured out that it is possible to use the single 50 Amp, 4-Pole outlet to achieve a Simultaneous 240 / 120 Volt Wiring Harness.Wire the male 240 V / 50 Amp plug properly. Green (ground) on top pole. Red & Black (hot) go to either of the side poles. White (common) goes to the bottom pole.220 Volt Outlet is wired without a common (white) wire. Connect the red & black wires to either side of the outlet. Also connect the green (ground) to the outlet.Using the white wire, go to the 110 volt outlets. Make certain that you connect the outlets (look on the back of the outlet) to the common pole.Using the black and or red (hot = 120 volts each) connect to the hot pole on the 120 volt outlets. Use ONLY one or the other per outlet or you will have 220 rather than 110.Ground all outlets using the green or bare wire.This is an isolated setup ( No Back-Feeding )and does not connect to any part of your home's wiring. In my case, I drilled a 3/4" hole through the wall and ran the main cable (8 gauge, 4 strand) outside making certain to leave plenty of slack to get to the generator while having enough left inside to make all my connections. I located the 1st connection (220 Volt) very close to the hole I drilled and mounted an outlet box to the wall for the A/C. Then I mounted a larger box beside it, to make my connections. From the larger box I have two smaller boxes connected using 12 gauge, 3-wire, to connect the 110 volt outlets.Check it out and maybe you can help others that have wanted / attempted to use more of the power that it harnessed in a larger generator like this one.I tested the setup with a 220V, 25,000 BTU A/C and several 110V items, including two shop-vacs. With everything going at the same time the voltage needle remained well within the operating range of approx. 220 Volts.Now that Irene is upon all of us on the eastern seaboard, I'm happy that I bought this generator. Even though I have not lost electricity yet, there are 900,000 people all around the area that have.

Not sure how humane it is to electrocute a mouse, but this thing reminds me of a terminator that came back in time to kill Sarah Connor -- it won't stop until it's target is dead. Well, or at least until the batteries run out.I truly had to chuckle at this thing -- it literally turns mouse catching into an automated process -- mouse steps in -- ZAP! -- then the electrocution chamber rotates, drops the mouse in a compartment, and rotates back into position, ready for its next victim.  A light even turns on when the "drawer" is full -- just pull it out, dispose of the rodents and slide the drawer back in for the next pile of vermin.  I'm not sure who needs a mouse trap that's this efficient and has such a large capacity.  If you have that many mice, it may be time to move!  For my purposes, I put it in the garage, and it did catch the one mouse we had. (Hopefully the only one.)Overall, I think it's pretty good at what it does and is about as "humane" as any other trap.  It's not like any of them safely capture mice so they can be set free in the wild.  Like all mouse traps, it's basically a killing machine.  But at least this one can be reused again and again, and emptied with little fuss or creepy-crawly feelings!  I agree, however, that this may cost a lot in batteries.  But I actually prefer battery operated, over plugging it into a wall outlet.  If you have mice, the trap needs to go where the mice are, not where the nearest outlet happens to be.  It certainly beats those old style traps that always snap my fingers!UPDATE 7/18/11 - Good News/Bad News --- this thing just caught another mouse; which means we have more mice than i thought. Eeeeeeew!

reviewText: I compost, recycle, reduce, reuse, buy recycled products, use flourescent bulbs and will be trying to install solar panels soon. Not a granola, just trying to be responsible about my life. So, the next logical step in my garden would be to stop using sevin dust and use an ecologoically responsible pesticide. Well, I am going back to sevin dust. My beautiful garden was destroyed overnight. My hubby sprayed this "pesticide" to my corn, squash, sweet potatoes, watermelon, and pumpkins. Woke up this morning and my corns are laying on the ground. No rain last night, so they were not blown over. Went to take a look and the corn has yellow stalks right from the middle down. Exactly where the insecticide instructed us to spray. The pumpkins have splashes of yellow where the insecticide landed on the leaves, the squash leaves are laying flat on the ground instead of springing gaily from the stalks witht he same yellow splashes. The last 6 weeks of work was for naught. Will be contacting the company and banging my head on a corporate beauracy for naught also. BTW, found a beautiful, healthy caterpillar laying next to a corn stalk. Looks like something survived...

This tape sticks to ITSELF much better than to copper pipe. The amount was ample for 15 feet of heat tape (I know it is confusing, but the heat tape is the black plastic covered heating element that this tape I am reviewing positions against the pipe to be heated). I applied it every six inches (sometimes 4 inches on pipe curves) and even had some left over.This tape has a backing. This paper backing must be removed prior to applying the tape to the pipe. This can be tricky in a crawl space because you have to pull each tape section (precutting sections makes applying easier and can be done before you get in the crawl space) off the backing and then apply it to the pipe and heat tape with the heat tape firmly against the pipe. It's impossible to do that with gloves on (you need the gloves for the insulation application later on). Make sure you circle the tape over itself to make sure it won't lose it's grip.Remember, the tape is the device that keeps your electrical element (heat tape) up against the pipe! If your heat tape has large gaps where it isn't touching properly, you will use more elctricity because it will take longer for the pipe to get to 45 degrees and the heat tape will wear out sooner because it's on more often. Don't skimp on applying this tape!Finally, do some math on the length of your pipe and how many strips of tape to precut BEFORE you get in the crawl space. Take the tape sections and the rest of the tape and some scissors in a small plastic bag with you. Everything you can do before you get in there helps.I'm 65 and was still sore for about three days after the job despite a lot of preplanning.

I can't think of anything I don't like about this yard tool.  I have a yard full of dandelions, and I had been using a small hand tool, which worked pretty well, but required that I either stoop or kneel, and if it was a plant with deep roots, it took some exertion, which I try to avoid, as I have a rib cage injury.  I read the product information, then many of the customer reviews, and I easily decided that this item was worth a try.  Honestly, I am so glad that I did, because it has made my life so much easier.  Most of the time, I can center it on the flowers the first time, then stepping on the peddle/lever closest to the blades, the blades will sink into the dirt quite easily.  It doesn't take much force, and you'll be able to feel that the blades have gone all the way into the dirt, and then you can immediately pull up on the handle, sliding your foot down to the end of the peddle/lever as you do so, and it's out, usually roots and all!  If you go off-center, you can usually repeat the process and extract the remainder.  It's actually kind of fun for a while, and the only time I have a problem, is when the dandelions grow in a cluster, then it sometimes takes me a little longer to judge their centers, but that's not the fault of the tool.  Because I'm using my hands, with the aid of my foot on the pedal/lever, there's kind of a pivot action going on, which eliminates all resistance on the part of the plant, so there is no exertion on my part, and nothing to bother my injury.  I would highly recommend this product.

I seeded approximately two to four seeds per pod so edge effects and inter-pod differences in climate control are very unlikely since not one pod germinated more than one seed. I.E. if it were a climate control problem any pod that produced 1 germinated seed should have seen germination from every seed in that pod. This was not the case. I had two germinated at pods on the edge of the flat and three in the middle of the flat. Two of the middle plants did not root.I did not check to see if there was PLS (pure live seed) test results on the product description. I won't purchase seed without a PLS test again.

I've been using this product for years. Yes, it does help in killing and controlling termite infestations. This is only a tool to kill and control the termites outside within the grounds around your home. You will also need to kill the nests within any wood structures as necessary...I recommendOrtho Home Defense Termite & Destructive Bug Killer - 32 oz. 0194260to treat and kill colonies in walls, floors and window frames. Look for toothpick sized holes dispersing wood particles. You may have to drill the hole larger and saturate with termite killer. I use a garden pump-sprayer with termite killer mixture and spray directly in the termite holes. Holes should be filled with caulking or re-plastered & re-painted to seal in termite killer. The killer should remain effective for years.I have a small apartment complex that had a serious termite infestation. I initially hired a professional which eliminated some termites but the infestation arose again the next year. When I called back for warranty re-treating, the professional did re-treat the areas originally treated but stated any other areas are new colonies and not covered by the warranty. Rather than spend hundreds more for a new treatment, I chose to educate myself on the life of the (btw blind) termite.Termites can live 25 years and must start a nest with two asexual termites. One becomes the male and one becomes the female queen. They reproduce drones with one purpose, to feed their queen. She remains stationary within the nest and can become 25 times larger in size...a real fat mama! If her male partner should die, one of the drones gets the privilege to be her new sexual boy-toy.Anyway, I learned subterranean termites need moisture to live and reproduce. These termites feed on plant/tree roots and then swarm (usually in seasonal hot weather) outside the ground and travel to nearby wood structures to form nests. These are the termites that destroy your home. These are the colonies that, most importantly, need to be controlled and killed.If you get the picture, the termite stakes are used to control and kill the subterranean termites outside your home and the spray mixture is used to control and kill the nests within wood.When I first used these stakes about 10 years ago, there was no "pop-up" indicator. I just know these were working since the swarms dissipated. These stakes last about a year killing termites unless there is an excessive amount of water washing away the chemical. Still, within the ground, the chemical helps kill termites. It did take me two (15) stake treatments in the course of 18 months to get the subterranean termites under control and several spray treatments in the various apartments and wood structures around the complex to get control of the termites. Now, I just watch for any new nests and treat accordingly.In closing, this product works to help kill and control termites.
summary: Subterranean Termite Killer...Helps to Kill/Control Termites & Ants

Wow! What can I say about this thing? I truly enjoy cutting my grass. Overall, I'm still pleased with it, but it has a few catches.1. Adjusting the blades seems to work best for me when I don't loosen the screws holding it all in place.  Just turning the adjusting screws works best for me.2. The springtime stalks that shoot up quickly from my grass are hard/impossible for this mower to deal with unless they're kept short.3. This mower does not deal with debris well, as mentioned in the manual.  I have hit some utility marker flag bits left behind and it sounds painful for the mower and causes some gouging of the blade.That said, here are its great qualities:1. My shoes don't turn green. I've cut grass at 6AM without upsetting the neighbors.3. No pollution.  Seriously.  Lawnmower engines have tended to pollute more in an hour than your car driving 600 miles. We bought a 16ft Intex Ultraframe last year and spent the entire summer rinsing and replacing cartridge filters and generally accepting a cloudy, sediment-y pool. Our well water is fairly hard and has enough iron to color the water. We used an iron out product and plenty of chlorine products but felt that the filter was our weak link. So this year we decided to upgrade (from 1200 gpm cartridge to 1600 gpm sand filter) and after only running it for a couple of days we are amazed at the pump power and clarity of the water.The setup was quite simple, we used the inlet and outlet mounts from the original pump (as they were identical) so we didn't have to lower the pool level. Basically filling the kettle with sand and fastening all the piping and control valve. Backwashed and rinsed new sand as per directions and started filtering within 10 minutes.After running for about 6 hours we needed to backwash (pressure gauge shows when it is needed) as our pool water was new and we had iron sediment to clean out from our Sequa-Sol treatment. Started to backwash and could not believe the "ick" that came out from the filter. Once it ran clear, we switched off and back to regular filter. The discharge power was back as strong as could be.This filter is amazing. Any doubts/concerns that we had about the expense being worth it are GONE. Cartridges are $5 a pop and we'd be lucky to get a week out of one, plus the original filter/pump was not keeping up anyway. This unit will pay for itself in only one summer and our water will finally be crystal clear.

I was tired of buying a disposable grill every three or four years and I was tired of running out of propane in the middle of the burn. So I went hunting for the best all-stainless natural gas portable out there, and I think I found it. For starters, the parent company, Onward Manufacturing, has been around about as long as me and has grown and morphed into one of the major contenders. They make and distribute other brands including Weber, but the Imperial line is the hands-down winner based an cost and features. And they're made in America.Everything except the cart box is solid stainless, including the double layer hood, the burners, reflectors and grates. It comes partially knocked down but is easily assembled with a #3 philips in about an hour. The instructions are all pictographic, so you don't need a degree in engineering to understand them. It comes complete with a back burner and rotisserie (both easily removed), three large drawers and even interior lights. The natural gas flex line and connections fittings are also included. I really don't think you'll find such a complete package until you approach the $2,000 range.My first few uses have been modest in scope, but the performance seems fine. There's a little front/back heat difference, but that's pretty common. The heat retention with the hood closed is impressive. The rotiserie roasts low and slow as you'd hope. Two large chickens took about an hour and were eavenly done.The $50 cover is worth the price, custom fit and heavy duty.

I have an approx. 50'x150' lot with house in center. The normal assortment of suburban trees, bushes, a swing set, raised garden, and detached garage. If I were reviewing the quality of yard I would give it a 2.5 out of 5. It is uneven, has 4-6 varieties of grasses and weeds each equally making up an equal percentage of the lawn. It has a small hill as well. Not the perfect set up for a push reel mower but certainly a perfect test for one.Set up was easy and it took me about 15 minutes. 11mm and 18mm socket are the only two tools needed. You build the handle and attach the small rear wheels and away you go. Mower itself is heavy, in a good way. Handle has several adjustment points and it worked well for me at 6'3" at the longest setting. The mower pushes easily. The blades on mine at least were perfectly adjusted out of the box. In addition to the paper instructions included, there is a video I saw on the Fiskars site showing you how to adjust the blades if needed. Unit seems to be very robust and of a good quality.I set mine to cut fairly high as the grass was longer and I didn't want to leave a trail of long cut grass to rake up. The mower worked very well with grass and weeds with-in a inch or so of the height setting. Stuff that was a bit longer, like dandelion flower shoots or long wispy grass it tended to miss some. Not so much of the grass but more so the dandelion shoots. Overall though it did quite well on all parts of the lawn. The nicer parts of the lawn with the thickest and nicest grass, it did the best on. My neighbor actually came over and looked at it when I was out and commented that it seemed to be doing a very nice job as well.It doesn't cut with the same width as my gas mower and it took my a couple of passes to get the set up right so I wasn't missing a small strip between rows. It also doesn't cut when you aren't push forward so areas under things where you can kind of stick a gas mower and move it around, were a bit harder to deal with. Ditto for going around trees as I found a straight forward motion worked best and going in a circle was possible, just a bit harder to maintain the blade spin. I will just need to weed whip a little more of the yard when using the reel mower. I also never had any problem with it getting an obstruction that stopped it at all, despite my lawn having a some twigs and sticks. That might have been to to the height setting, but I could every so often hear something getting crunched and the mower blades kept on spinning.It is very quiet and less messy then a gas mower. I wore a pair of flip flops and my legs were very clean afterwards and the shoes didn't pick up any green staining like you would see after using a gas mower. Same workout to push around as the gas mower I have (non assisted type) but that isn't a bad thing as I enjoy the exercise. Having done the lawn once now, it did come out looking good overall even if it left some of the dandelion stalks. I do think I will be more prone to grabbing it on short notice and pushing it around to stay on top of things vs. the gas mower just because it is so simple and quiet. It won't replace my gas mower for 100% of my mowings, but it will be doing the vast majority of them going forward. Overall very happy to have it and would recommend it.Update: Have used it three times now without using the gas mower in between. It is doing a great job. Was able to get out this morning at 0730 and get the yard done without worrying about waking the neighbors. Can also talk to my daughter who likes to walk along side me.
summary: Quiet, easy to push, and works well

reviewText: No program disk is included and you are instructed to download the software from their website. So much for an easy setup. You will have to give them all your personal information in registrating the product before they will send you the software via e-mail. You will have to find UPC codes and serial numbers as well. After you install new batteries in the floating sensor and plug the reciever, you will be instructed to wait for the "signal bar" to register full strength. Unfortunatly, I only recieved a signal strength of 68% while holding the sensor near the reciever. Once I put the sensor in the pool less than 15 feet away, I was now getting a signal strength of 53%. It was now transmitting the pool temp, ORP, and PH. There was no chlorine reading, just a blank line. Everything else looked right, but it would now require a 4 hour "stabilization process". The process lasted for two hours and then lost the signal from the sensor and it was in a state of permanent limbo. It's pretty obvious this thing has a poor transmitter with little or no range. I never did get a chlorine reading and I wasted a whole Sunday on this stupid thing. The toll free customer assistance is Monday thru Friday 9am to 5pm. I'll be at work during those times, so that's not helpful at all. There are plenty of calibration settings were you can reset the radio transmission and recalibrate each reading, but it warns you it is only for "advanced users".The idea of this product is very neat, but obviously it's more trouble than it's worth. The final product was poorly tested and some of the working components are not reliable. I wish these companies would realize that consumers want products that work right out of the box. It's just taking up space in my pool and doing nothing.
summary: Don't waste your money! This thing doesn't work!

I have several bird feeders (suet, thistle, seed, etc.) in my yard here in Connecticut and I get a tremendous number and variety of birds. I always feel a bit guilty though that I don't pay enough attention to their water needs and it can get hot and dry here by July. I have a bird bath, but I'm not great at keeping it filled. For those reasons, this little water cooler for birds really appealed to me.I have to say I'm more than pleased with the quality and the design. First, it's very rugged and I don't think that, even if it fell from the hook where I have it hanging, that it would get hurt. Also, its very simple to use--just unscrew the base, fill it with water, re-attach the base and (quickly) flip it right-side up and you're ready to go. It's that easy. And the threads are very strong and the dish part screws on very securely.The loop at the top of the bottle makes it easy to hang. I used one of those elongated s-hooks that are used to hang a hanging pot from a branch or whatever and it works perfectly. A piece of nylon fishing line would work fine, too.I really am very pleased with this and I think it will be a hit with the birds (I just put it out today, so still waiting for the first customers). I'm hanging it next to my screened porch to keep the cats entertained. It's nice to find an affordable product like this that does what it says it will do, is nicely made and serves a good purpose. A great gift for your bird-feeding friends, too. I'll post some photos once the birds belly up to the bar.By the way, a few reviewers have said that they have had it up for a while and no takers yet. I suggest posting a sign nearby, pointing to the waterer. (Kidding.) It takes a little while for birds to feel safe around anything new in your yard. They see it, they know it's there, they'll come. If you want to attract them faster, try letting a hose drip into a bucket nearby for a few hours a day for a few days--birds are extremely attracted to moving water. If they think water is in the area, they will investigate more.
summary: This is a great idea, I love it & so nicely made!

As stated above, I live in North Central Wisconsin, with all the winter weather adventures that this entails.  This little guy is great for just about anything you're going to need it for.Now that I have an entire winter under my belt with the Snow Joe, I can honestly say that it performed well above what I ever expected from a plastic, electric unit.  We got some pretty impressive snows, last winter, up to 26 inches at a time of wet and heavy snow.  The fist time we got 12 inches, I expected to have to call my brother-in-law and have him lend me his gas unit.  But the Snow Joe handled it.  I had to take two passes to get the full 12 inches, taking about 6 inches, then backing up and getting it clean to the concrete.  But compared to a shovel, or a the hassle and cost of a two stage gas unit, it was great.  It even handled the packed and frozen stuff the city plow leaves in front of the curbside mailbox.  It's so light that if I need to reposition it, I just pick it up and carry it to the next place.  As far as cord issues, I find that this is really no more hassle than you have while vacuuming, and once you work out a system for your particular drive/sidewalk, it gets second nature.  I did store the unit in the house, since it was small enough.  I just put down a garbage bag, with an old towel on top, to catch the melt.  By the end of the 2012/2013 winter, the snow piles in our boulevard were to tall for me to see over, at 6'1" tall, and our mailbox was accessed through a little hole we'd dug into that snow bank.  The Snow Joe had thrown all of it there, including the heavy piles left by the plow.  I worked it well above what the designers meant it to do, I'm sure, but it handled it.  Other than an occasional scratch from the odd rock and a missing sticker, or two, it barely looks used.Recommended, whole-heartedly, by this Wisconsinite, who's happy to no longer have to break his back, shoveling.

This thing is AWESOME!. I've been messing around with several different cold smoke generators and none of them really worked well. This thing works really super!  I wasted too much money and time on those other things.After following the directions to "season" the tube and burn off left over oil from manufacturing, I put a couple pounds of cheese in my Masterbuilt Electric smoker and the Tube Smoker in the bottom.  I filled the Tube Smoker half full of pellets and fired it up.I DID NOT use any heat from the smoker itself for this test.  In fact I never plugged it in. The cheese will melt at just over 100 deg (F).  I wanted to see how much heat the Tube Smoker would generate because I want to use it for cold smoking.  I have a larger barrel style smoker I normally use for cold smoking because the heat source is well away from the food to be smoked.  Trying it in this smaller unit was just a test.The pellets lasted about 2.5 hours (half full).  There was enough heat generated to cause the cheese to soften but not melt.  I didn't think to put a thermometer inside so I don't know the exact temp.If I were to use the Tube Smoker in a BBQ grill for example, I would make sure the food to be smoked was as low as possible and plenty of air flow.  It does generate too much heat for a small, closed in space for cold smoking.It would work great in a BBQ grill to add smoke to your food.  If you're cooking steak, burgers, chicken.  I like to throw a couple pieces of Tri Tip (tied together) on the rotisserie and add wood chips to the coals.  I plan  to use the Tube Smoker next time in the BBQ.This is a really wonderful product and for price and my needs, I prefer it over the A-MAZE-N Smoker.  That's the "maze" style, wood dust smoker.  Such a simple but useful idea.

I was worried about purchasing these after I read some of the reviews, but figured I knew enough about plants and terra cotta to make them work :) First, I submerged the Plant Nanny in water and let it soak for an hour or so. Terra cotta absorbs a lot of water, and I figured if the stakes were already full of moisture when placed into the dirt, they would be less likely to pull in moisture from the bottles as quickly. Then, I gave my plants (I use these on tomato plants) a healthy watering - almost 2x as much as I normally would on a regular water - to really soak the soil. Goal Zero is great a putting together comprehensive, easy to use solar solutions that actually work and this latest "Goal Zero 41022 Guide 10 Plus Solar Recharging Kit" is no exception.This is their smallest/lightest comprehensive kit thats great for hiking or camping or for an emergency bag.  Its primarily meant to help power or charge small mobile USB, AA or AAA devices like phones, small tablet computers, flashlights, radios etc and offers a great solution for those away from normal power sources beyond their devices battery life.It consists of:1) A Nomad 7 Solar panel.  This consists of two rigid 3.5 watt high efficiency solar panels in a sturdy folding ballistic nylon frame (kind of like a wallet but bigger) that contains the electronics and power connections along with a zippered mesh pouch on the back of one panel that can hold the rest of the kit and more.  The panel has a flap with a magnetic closure and several cord loops in various positions to allow you to hang or fasten the panel to something.2) The Gide 10 Plus Recharger.  This is a small plastic box that holds 4 NiMh Rechargeable AA batteries (included) (or 4 AAA batteries - not included) that can charge the batteries to accumulate and store the power from the solar panel, and then provide higher levels of consistent power to your USB devices.3) 4 AA Rechargeable 2300mah 1.2v NiMh Goal Zero branded batteries.  These have good capacity but as the instructions say to make sure to charge them every few months, they are likely not low self discharge (LSD) batteries like Sanyo Eneloops that can retain 75% of their charge after 3 years.4) An AAA adapter5) A 12v female cigarette lighter cable to allow the panel to directly power some 12 volt devicesEverything fits in the mesh compartment on the back of the solar panel and it forms a package about 7"x9"x1.5" and weighing about 1lb 11oz.  There's plenty of room left in the pouch for the USB cables of whatever devices you might want to charge/power with this kit, more batteries etc and you'll still likely end up under 2 pounds.So what's good about this kit?  First off, its a kit thats easy to use, well designed and constructed, and contains all the bits an pieces you'll need (other than the USB cables specific to your devices).  As the panel is small and sunlight varies in strength the panel itself won't always consistently charge or power devices directly - so a power pack is included to accumulate/normalize/amplify that power and also make it available to USB devices when the sun isn't out.  And it doubles as a battery charger for AA or AAA batteries (although you have to charge 4 at a time).This is one of my favorite kits and I give it 4 stars.  Why only 4?  Well it is a bit bigger and heavier than it needs to be (see the PowerFilm AA and AA+USB units if you want the ultimate in tiny and light - but they are not as versatile).  The battery pack doesn't independently charge each battery but requires a set of 4 to charge anything.  The particular panel technology used is the most efficient in strong sunlight but in less ideal conditions it looses efficiency quickly (the PowerFilm panels are not as efficient in full sunlight but are much more efficient in less ideal conditions).I highly recommend this kit for an individual thats going to be "off grid" for a while that wants to continue to use a few small USB or AA or AAA devices.  If you have a lot of devices or want to power things for more than one person you might want to consider a bigger kit like the Sherpa 50.
summary: Great for Hiking, Camping and Emergency use of small USB or AA or AAA powered devices

reviewText: I have been using Springpad for about 2 years.  It is my most used (besides email, facebook, texting).  I have added all my favorite recipes to it.  That is my favorite thing about it. If I am at the store and decide to cook something, go to the app, look up the recipe and see what I need to buy.  If Cooking Light sends me a recipe on my email and I think I may want to cook it, I spring it into the Cooking Light notebook.I also use it for planning.  For Thanksgiving, I made a notebook called Thanksgiving.  Went to find my recipes and added to the notebook.  I add a shopping list (which is amazing part of springpad too), added a checklist of things to make, added a checklist of stuff to organize and get before hand (tablecloths, napkins, etc.)  I went to NYC and made a board of everything I wanted to do.  Saved my reservation numbers, addresses of places, etc in that notebook.The best way to get to know springpad is to watch their tutorials.  You will wonder how you got along without it.  I have tried other apps like this, and this is the best.

I've tried two other calendar apps but I didn't like their limits.  This does absolutely everything you need a calendar to do. Plus it has tasks and agenda included.  Yes for an app it is "pricey" at six bucks...Lol.  But you can't put a price on how efficient and organized it makes you.Yes it took me a while to get it set up with each view (day, week, month,year, task, and agenda) appearing with the beautiful and vibrant color combos I chose that were unique to that view.  But once you have that done it is a cinch. So many options of colors and types of reminders that it's impossible not to end up with the calendar that makes you smile every time you use it. For the most basic math of the form A op B, this calculator is functional.  And this is, of course, what a lot of people do.However, as pointed out a few times already, any calculator which claims to have a scientific (or even business) mode and doesn't follow the correct order of operations has clearly dropped the ball.Personally, I stick with Droid48 (on the Android market) for all of my calculator needs, big and small.  It emulates an HP-48GX calculator, provides a near identical skin, and even runs the actual 48GX ROM.  It's as close to the real thing as you can get without holding the real hardware.  If you're not a fan of RPN (Reverse Polish Notation), then you probably won't like this, which is really too bad.  You should definitely try it.  It's even small!

reviewText: This app works and looks great on the Kindle Fire. In-Depth:Overview:Besides the basic four functions; this calculator also has the three trigonometric functions, exponents and logs, the tip calculator, a calculation history, and the standard memory feature. The app also takes advantage of the fact that it's on the tablet by letting you pick the visual theme. There are two types of themes, 3D and stranded - and each has several color schemes. The tip calculator has one 3D and one standard color schemes, and the main calculator has six 3D and eight standard color schemes. The 3D themes are what you see an example of on the icon. They look really nice on the 7" display, with crisp buttons and a calculator-like panel in the background. The standard themes switch out for just rectangular buttons on a solid background. Simple, and if you have vision problems this will make it a breeze to use, plus some of these look nice as well. I personally like the 3D themes, but I'm sure some people will like the more basic themes as well.Permissions/Performance:This app doesn't need any permissions, which is awesome. And you can easily shut it down from the app menu. No need for force-stopping.  :)Why I took off a star:1) You cannot have the advanced functions (exp, log, etc) unless you close the history panel on the bottom. Also, with all the buttons displayed, they. don't. quite. fit. on the screen. You can still use them, but it enough the scrolling is activated - a minor annoyance, but one that should have been fixed. It really is just a millimeter off from fitting the screen perfectly.2) The calculator only works from one angle. So you cannot rotate it. Again, it works fine just like it is, but I would have liked the option to use the app in landscape mode.
